text: 58-year-old female. The patient has been treated for community-acquired pneumonia with levofloxacin on the medical floor. She reports developing watery diarrhea with at least 9 episodes within the last two days, accompanied by lower abdominal discomfort and cramping.

speaker: Doctor
text: The CBC indicates neutrophilic leukocytosis, suggesting an active infection. Given your history of recent levofloxacin use and watery diarrhea, we must prioritize ruling out *C. difficile* colitis over a urinary tract infection, which does not typically present with these gastrointestinal symptoms. REQUEST TEST: Stool_CDAD_Toxin. How many bowel movements are you passing per day?

speaker: Doctor
text: The Stool CDAD toxin result is currently not specified, so we cannot yet confirm *C. difficile* infection. Given your recent levofloxacin use and the high frequency of your bowel movements, this remains the primary concern. Please tell me if you have experienced any recent antibiotic use before the current course, or any travel to areas with poor sanitation?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Watery diarrhea. I also have Lower abdominal discomfort, Abdominal cramping.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: *Clostridioides difficile* colitis. The clinical presentation of acute watery diarrhea, abdominal cramping, and significant neutrophilic leukocytosis following recent levofloxacin therapy is highly suggestive of antibiotic-associated colitis. Given the pending CDAD toxin result and the high pre-test probability, immediate management with oral vancomycin or fidaxomicin is indicated, and I will request your medical images to evaluate for pseudomembranes.
